Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: ECG 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) and ECG 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR intervals ranging 0.35-0.72 s) with no discernible organised P waves, i.e. atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response at about 139 and 144 bpm respectively. An unspecified atrial fibrillation diagnosis was recorded at the same encounter. The documented rhythm and rate are both inconsistent with the tracings and need clinical reconciliation.

Patient is taking escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication (current clinic order 2026-07-18 to 2026-12-26, continuously prescribed since 2024). His most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT about 500 ms and Bazett-corrected QTc about 535 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. Most recent electrolytes are not contributory (potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL, both 2026-03-18). Of note, the 5/14/2024 note that started escitalopram described this same tracing as having an acceptable QT.

Patient is on citalopram 40 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication (current clinic order 2026-07-15 to 2027-01-07; citalopram has been continued since 2023). Her most recent ECG (104821039, 2023-11-10) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT about 495-500 ms and Bazett QTc about 534 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. Note also that 40 mg daily exceeds the labelled maximum citalopram dose because of dose-dependent QT prolongation. Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (2026-07-15) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (2025-03-08) are normal.

95-year-old woman on amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication (current clinic order 2026-06-17 to 2027-01-06). Her most recent ECG (101515306, 2022-04-27) shows sinus bradycardia at 57 bpm with a markedly prolonged QT of about 595 ms and Bazett QTc about 583 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. Most recent potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (both 2026-06-17) are within range, so the prolongation is not explained by electrolytes; she is also on metoprolol, and no ECG has been repeated in over four years.

interpretations.explanation: Most recent (and only) ECG, 2026-03-07. Regular narrow-complex rhythm at about 81 bpm with a consistent upright P wave in lead II before every QRS (P amplitude ~200 uV, beat-to-beat P correlation 0.99) and PR about 180 ms, i.e. normal sinus rhythm with mild sinus arrhythmia (RR 0.66-0.86 s). QRS duration 80 ms with no bundle branch block pattern; frontal QRS axis about +45 degrees (normal). QT about 335 ms at RR 0.74 s gives a Bazett QTc of roughly 390 ms, normal. No prior ECG is available for comparison. Notable because the same-day clinic note reports sinus rhythm, which this tracing confirms, despite a history of atrial fibrillation.

ECG of 2025-07-15. Regular rhythm at about 104 bpm (RR 0.58 s) with a prominent upright P wave in lead II before every QRS (P amplitude ~215 uV, P correlation 0.98) and PR about 140 ms: sinus tachycardia. QRS 94 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +38 degrees (normal). QT about 325 ms, Bazett QTc about 428 ms, normal. The prior ECG 100698634 (2025-06-20) was sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm with QRS 90 ms and QTc about 410 ms; rhythm, conduction and QTc are unchanged apart from the slower rate. Notably, despite documented paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, both tracings are in sinus rhythm.

ECG of 2024-05-21, the only tracing available. Regular rhythm at about 109 bpm (RR 0.55 s) with a consistent upright P wave in lead II before each QRS and PR about 130 ms: sinus tachycardia. QRS 90 ms, narrow, with no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +35 degrees (normal). QT about 315 ms, Bazett QTc about 424 ms, normal. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 2026-06-10 19:36, the later of two tracings that day. The ventricular response is irregularly irregular (RR intervals 0.35-0.65 s) at an average rate of about 144 bpm, with no organised P waves (pre-QRS atrial deflection ~70 uV with poor beat-to-beat reproducibility, correlation 0.45) and a fibrillatory baseline: atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response. No measurable PR interval. QRS 92 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +3 degrees (normal). QT about 290 ms, Bazett QTc about 450 ms. The earlier tracing the same day, 107914094 (17:13), showed the same rhythm - atrial fibrillation at about 139 bpm with QRS 96 ms and QTc about 450 ms - so there are no interval changes. The clinic note of the same day describing normal sinus rhythm at 72 bpm conflicts with both tracings.

ECG of 2025-08-02. Regular rhythm at about 69 bpm (RR 0.87 s, coefficient of variation 0.01) with a low-amplitude atrial deflection preceding every QRS at a fixed PR of about 125 ms; the P wave is positive in leads I and aVL but negative in II, III and aVF, suggesting a low atrial pacemaker rather than a high right atrial focus, but the rhythm is regular, 1:1 conducted and physiological. QRS 78 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about -25 degrees (normal, borderline leftward). QT about 405 ms, Bazett QTc about 435 ms, normal. The prior ECG 104232242 (2025-04-27) had the same rate-corrected intervals (QRS 78 ms, QTc about 411 ms) but showed a globally inverted limb-lead pattern consistent with arm-lead reversal; there are no qualifying changes between the tracings.

ECG of 2024-05-23, the only tracing available. Regular rhythm at about 97 bpm (RR 0.62 s) with a reproducible upright P wave in lead II before every QRS and PR about 120 ms: sinus rhythm at the upper limit of normal rate. QRS 76 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block pattern; frontal QRS axis about 0 degrees (normal). QT about 290 ms, Bazett QTc about 367 ms, normal. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 2025-12-25, the only tracing available. Regular rhythm at about 72 bpm (RR 0.83 s) with an upright P wave in lead II before every QRS and PR about 130-145 ms: normal sinus rhythm. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +22 degrees (normal). QT about 385 ms, Bazett QTc about 421 ms, normal. No prior ECG for comparison. This tracing predates the escitalopram started 2026-08-01 and therefore cannot serve as the post-initiation ECG required by clinic policy.

ECG of 2024-11-15. The ventricular response is irregularly irregular (RR intervals 0.69-1.16 s, RMSSD 288 ms) with no organised P waves - the pre-QRS atrial deflection is only about 35 uV and is not reproducible from beat to beat (correlation 0.31) - indicating atrial fibrillation with a slow ventricular response averaging about 53 bpm. No measurable PR interval. QRS 90 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +29 degrees (normal). QT about 440 ms at this slow rate, Bazett QTc about 414 ms, normal. The prior ECG 107873952 (2024-11-12) was regular sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with a well-formed 220 uV P wave and PR about 160 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new since that tracing (NEW_AF). The QTc is essentially unchanged.

ECG of 2025-03-09. Regular rhythm at about 58 bpm (RR 1.03 s) with a reproducible upright P wave in lead II before each QRS (P correlation 1.00) and PR about 110 ms: sinus bradycardia. QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +61 degrees (normal). QT about 445 ms at this slow rate, Bazett QTc about 437 ms, within normal limits. The prior ECG 106045460 (2025-03-08) was nearly identical (sinus rhythm 62 bpm, QRS 86 ms, QTc about 455 ms), so there are no qualifying changes. This tracing predates the haloperidol started 2026-09-15.

ECG of 2025-08-23, the only tracing available. Regular rhythm at about 83 bpm (RR 0.72 s, coefficient of variation <0.01) with an upright P wave in lead II before every QRS and PR about 140 ms: normal sinus rhythm. QRS 72 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +54 degrees (normal). QT about 340 ms, Bazett QTc about 401 ms, normal. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 2020-06-19. Regular rhythm at about 77 bpm (RR 0.78 s) with a large upright P wave in lead II before every QRS (about 265 uV) and PR about 148 ms: normal sinus rhythm. QRS 74 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +65 degrees (normal). QT about 385 ms, Bazett QTc about 436 ms, normal. The prior ECG 109048192 (2020-02-02) was sinus rhythm at 75 bpm but with a wider QRS of about 114 ms (still below the 120 ms criterion for bundle branch block) and a markedly prolonged QT with QTc about 590 ms. The QTc has therefore fallen by more than 60 ms (QTC_DECREASE_60); no bundle branch block is present on either tracing.

ECG of 2021-01-18. Regular rhythm at about 120 bpm (RR 0.50 s, essentially no variability) with a discrete upright P wave preceding every QRS in lead II and a biphasic P in V1; PR about 170 ms. This is sinus tachycardia. QRS 92 ms without a bundle branch block pattern; frontal axis about +50 degrees (normal). QT about 260 ms, Bazett QTc about 371 ms, normal. Compared with the prior tracing 106186980 (2016-09-16, sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, QRS 90 ms, QTc about 375 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

ECG of 2025-06-23. Regular rhythm at about 54 bpm (RR 1.10 s) with a broad upright P wave in lead II before every QRS and a prolonged PR interval of about 210-225 ms, i.e. sinus bradycardia with first-degree atrioventricular block. QRS 82 ms, narrow, with no bundle branch block (prominent q waves inferiorly and tall R waves in V3-V5 but normal duration); frontal QRS axis about 0 degrees (normal). QT about 405 ms, Bazett QTc about 387 ms, normal. The prior ECG 103042067 (2024-11-30) showed sinus bradycardia at 51 bpm with PR about 182 ms, QRS 84 ms and QTc about 377 ms; the PR has lengthened slightly into the first-degree block range, but none of the listed change categories apply.

ECG of 2025-09-13. Markedly irregular ventricular response (RR intervals 0.29-0.58 s, coefficient of variation 0.19) at an average rate of about 152 bpm, with no discernible P waves at all (pre-QRS atrial signal about 10 uV, beat-to-beat correlation 0.12): atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response. No measurable PR interval. QRS 100 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about -22 degrees (normal). QT about 255 ms, Bazett QTc about 408 ms, normal. The prior ECG 107374881 (2025-09-12, the day before) showed a regular rhythm at about 77 bpm with visible P waves and PR about 130 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new (NEW_AF); QTc is essentially unchanged.

ECG of 2025-11-23. Regular rhythm at about 73 bpm (RR 0.82 s) with a well-formed upright P wave in lead II before every QRS (about 220 uV, correlation 0.99) and PR about 165 ms: normal sinus rhythm, confirming the same-day clinic note. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +10 degrees (normal). QT about 360 ms, Bazett QTc about 396 ms, normal. The prior ECG 105362569 (2025-11-21) was also sinus rhythm (67 bpm, QRS 88 ms) but with QT about 500 ms and QTc about 527 ms, so the QTc has fallen by more than 60 ms (QTC_DECREASE_60).

ECG of 2025-02-15, the only tracing available. Regular rhythm at about 74 bpm (RR 0.81 s) with an upright P wave in lead II before every QRS and PR about 185-190 ms, at the upper limit of normal but not meeting criteria for first-degree AV block: normal sinus rhythm. QRS 88 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +61 degrees (normal). QT about 380 ms, Bazett QTc about 421 ms, normal. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 2023-06-26. Regular rhythm at about 112 bpm (RR 0.538 s with almost no variability) with a single upright P wave in leads II, III and aVF before each QRS, an isoelectric PR segment and PR about 175 ms; there is no sawtooth flutter baseline and no second atrial deflection in the ST segment, so this is sinus tachycardia rather than atrial flutter despite the documented flutter history. QRS 94 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +35 degrees (normal). QT about 280 ms, Bazett QTc about 379 ms, normal. The prior ECG 102955795 (2022-07-04) was essentially identical (sinus tachycardia 115 bpm, QRS 94 ms, QTc about 376 ms), so there are no changes.

ECG of 2025-03-14, the only tracing available. Underlying rhythm is regular at about 61 bpm (RR 0.98 s) with a broad upright P wave in lead II before each QRS and PR about 190 ms: sinus rhythm; a single premature beat with a compensatory pause accounts for the isolated short-long RR sequence and for the high RMSSD, and there is no fibrillatory baseline, so this tracing is not in atrial fibrillation despite the documented paroxysmal AF. QRS 98 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about -31 degrees (left axis deviation). QT about 385 ms, Bazett QTc about 388 ms, normal. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 2026-04-29, the only tracing available. Regular rhythm at about 69 bpm (RR 0.86 s) with a small, reproducible atrial deflection before each QRS at a fixed PR of about 135 ms: sinus rhythm. QRS 92 ms, narrow, with no bundle branch block. The frontal plane is strikingly abnormal: the P wave, QRS and T are all negative in lead I and lead II and positive in aVR, giving a measured frontal QRS axis of about -173 degrees (extreme axis); the precordial R-wave progression is normal, so this pattern most likely reflects right/left arm lead reversal rather than true extreme axis deviation or dextrocardia, and repeating the tracing with correct lead placement is advised. QT about 365 ms, Bazett QTc about 391 ms, normal. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 2023-11-10. Regular rhythm at about 70 bpm (RR 0.86 s) with an upright P wave in lead II before every QRS and PR about 150-165 ms: normal sinus rhythm. QRS 96 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +42 degrees (normal). The T waves are broad and prolonged with QT about 495 ms and Bazett QTc about 534 ms, clearly prolonged. The prior ECG 107149156 (2020-06-17) showed sinus tachycardia at 133 bpm with QT about 275 ms and QTc about 411 ms, so the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60). She remains on citalopram 40 mg daily.

ECG of 2026-03-08, the only tracing available. Regular rhythm at about 68 bpm (RR 0.88 s) with an upright P wave in lead II before every QRS and PR about 135-150 ms: normal sinus rhythm. QRS 84 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +57 degrees (normal). There is repolarisation abnormality with T-wave inversion in I, V2, V5 and V6 and a deeply negative T in V2-V3; measured QT is about 410-420 ms and the Bazett QTc is about 440 ms, i.e. borderline but below the 500 ms clinic threshold. No prior ECG for comparison. This is the post-initiation ECG for escitalopram started 2026-02-12.

ECG of 2019-01-13. Regular rhythm at about 53 bpm (RR 1.13 s) with an upright P wave in lead II before every QRS and PR about 165 ms: sinus bradycardia. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about -5 degrees (normal). QT about 380 ms, Bazett QTc about 355 ms, normal. The prior ECG 108651109 (2018-12-13) was sinus rhythm at 66 bpm with QRS 98 ms and QTc about 397 ms; the QTc change is about 40 ms, below the 60 ms threshold, and there are no other qualifying changes.

ECG of 2023-10-08. Regular sinus rhythm at about 68 bpm (RR 0.88 s) with a uniform upright P wave in lead II before each QRS and PR about 130-145 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +50 degrees (normal). The T waves are broad and late-peaking with QT about 500 ms, giving a Bazett QTc of roughly 535 ms, which is markedly prolonged. The previous ECG 100065910 (2022-11-23) was sinus rhythm at 74 bpm with QT about 330 ms and QTc about 365 ms, so the QTc has increased by well over 60 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60). This is the patient's most recent tracing and he remains on escitalopram, a QT watch-list drug.

ECG of 2022-07-13. The rhythm is now regular (RR 0.40-0.45 s, coefficient of variation 0.02) at about 141 bpm, with a reproducible low-amplitude P wave preceding each QRS and an isoelectric segment before the QRS; this is sinus tachycardia. No pacing spikes are present despite the documented pacemaker. QRS 84 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about 0 degrees (normal). QT about 270 ms, Bazett QTc about 417 ms, normal. The prior ECG 109839112 (2022-07-11) showed an irregularly irregular rhythm at about 110 bpm with no organised P waves (atrial signal about 30 uV, beat-to-beat correlation 0.41), i.e. atrial fibrillation; that atrial fibrillation has resolved on the present tracing (RESOLVED_AF). QTc is unchanged.

ECG of 2025-05-12, the only tracing available. Regular rhythm at about 82 bpm (RR 0.73 s) with an upright P wave in lead II before every QRS (correlation 0.98) and PR about 140-155 ms: normal sinus rhythm. QRS duration is about 104 ms - a nonspecific intraventricular conduction delay but below the 120 ms threshold, and without an RBBB or LBBB pattern. Frontal QRS axis about +33 degrees (normal). QT about 375 ms, Bazett QTc about 438 ms, normal. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 2022-07-16. Regular rhythm at about 91 bpm (RR 0.66 s) with a consistent upright P wave in lead II before every QRS (correlation 1.00) and PR about 165-185 ms: normal sinus rhythm. QRS 80 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about -17 degrees (normal). QT about 340 ms, Bazett QTc about 421 ms, normal. The prior ECG 102616671 (2021-05-16) was sinus rhythm at 87 bpm with QRS 84 ms and QTc about 403 ms, so there are no qualifying changes.

ECG of 2024-07-17. Regular rhythm at about 61 bpm (RR 0.98 s) with an upright P wave in lead II before every QRS and a prolonged PR of about 215-230 ms: sinus rhythm with first-degree atrioventricular block. The QRS is wide at about 132 ms with a broad monophasic R wave in leads I, aVL and V6, absence of q waves laterally and a QS complex in V1-V3 - a left bundle branch block pattern - with secondary ST-T changes. Frontal QRS axis about -20 degrees (normal). QT about 450 ms, Bazett QTc about 452 ms, mildly prolonged but below the 500 ms threshold. The prior ECG 103686933 (2024-06-03) showed the same findings (sinus rhythm 68 bpm, PR about 212 ms, QRS 130 ms with LBBB, QTc about 437 ms), so the bundle branch block is not new and there are no qualifying changes.

ECG of 2025-03-19. Regular rhythm at about 102 bpm (RR 0.59 s) with an upright P wave in lead II before every QRS (correlation 0.99) and PR about 135 ms: sinus tachycardia. QRS 88 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +45 degrees (normal). QT about 320 ms, Bazett QTc about 414 ms, normal. The prior ECG 101016166 (2025-03-18) was essentially identical (sinus tachycardia 102 bpm, QRS 84 ms, QTc about 414 ms), so there are no changes.

ECG of 2025-09-22, the only tracing available. Regular rhythm at about 66 bpm (RR 0.91 s) with an upright P wave in lead II before every QRS and PR about 150 ms: normal sinus rhythm. QRS 90 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about -19 degrees (normal). QT about 375 ms, Bazett QTc about 394 ms, normal. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 2024-04-19, the only tracing available. Regular rhythm at about 120 bpm (RR 0.50 s, coefficient of variation <0.01) with a consistent upright P wave in lead II before every QRS and PR about 135 ms: sinus tachycardia. QRS 78 ms, narrow, with no bundle branch block or fascicular pattern; frontal QRS axis about +69 degrees (normal). QT about 250 ms; Bazett QTc about 354 ms, normal. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 2021-08-23 (the later of two tracings recorded the same day). Regular rhythm at about 101 bpm with an upright P wave in lead II preceding every QRS (P amplitude ~180 uV, P correlation 0.99) and PR about 135 ms: sinus tachycardia. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +59 degrees (normal). QT about 310 ms, Bazett QTc about 400 ms, normal. The immediately preceding tracing 102910502 from the same day was essentially identical (sinus tachycardia 100 bpm, QRS 88 ms, QTc about 396 ms), so there are no interval change.

ECG of 2024-10-24. Regular rhythm at about 52 bpm (RR 1.15-1.18 s) with an upright P wave in lead II before each QRS and PR about 168 ms: sinus bradycardia. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +36 degrees (normal). QT about 440 ms at this slow rate, Bazett QTc about 407 ms, normal. The prior ECG 104629882 (2023-05-22) showed sinus rhythm at 57 bpm with one premature beat, QRS 84 ms and QTc about 393 ms; there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc. Importantly, despite a documented history of atrial fibrillation, this tracing is in sinus rhythm.

ECG of 2024-12-05 (second tracing that day). Rhythm is sinus tachycardia at about 121 bpm (RR 0.49 s) with an upright P wave in lead II before each conducted beat and PR about 150 ms; there is one premature beat with a short coupling interval. The QRS is now narrow at 90 ms with no bundle branch block. The frontal QRS axis is about +144 degrees (right axis deviation: QRS is net negative in lead I and net positive in aVF). QT about 280 ms, Bazett QTc about 400 ms, normal. The earlier tracing the same day, 106516875, showed a wide-complex rhythm at 100 bpm with a QRS of about 150 ms, a tall monophasic R wave in V1, deeply negative QRS in I/V6 and an extreme frontal axis (about -170 degrees) - a right bundle branch block type intraventricular conduction delay. That wide-complex conduction abnormality has resolved on the present tracing (RESOLVED_BUNDLE_BRANCH_BLOCK); the QTc is unchanged (about 425 to 400 ms).

ECG of 2025-11-24. Regular rhythm at about 62 bpm (RR 0.97 s) with an upright P wave in lead II before each QRS and PR about 165 ms: normal sinus rhythm; despite a history of atrial fibrillation this tracing is not in AF. QRS 96 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +67 degrees (normal). The repolarisation is markedly prolonged, with a very broad T wave, QT about 555 ms and Bazett QTc about 565 ms. The prior ECG 108780865 (2025-06-07) showed sinus bradycardia at 47 bpm with QT about 475 ms and QTc about 420 ms, so the QTc has risen by about 145 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60). The interval change coincides with amiodarone started at the 2025-11-10 clinic visit.

ECG of 2024-09-17, the only tracing available. The rhythm is irregularly irregular (RR intervals 0.39-1.09 s, coefficient of variation 0.29, RMSSD 264 ms) with no organised P waves before the QRS complexes (pre-QRS atrial deflection only ~50 uV and poorly reproducible between beats, beat-to-beat correlation 0.48) and a fibrillatory baseline: atrial fibrillation with an average ventricular rate of about 99 bpm. No measurable PR interval. QRS 82 ms, narrow, without bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about -52 degrees (left axis deviation). QT about 320 ms, Bazett QTc about 411 ms, normal. No prior ECG for comparison. The AF is consistent with the recorded diagnosis; the patient is on warfarin.

arguments.explanation: ECG of 2022-04-27, the most recent tracing for this 95-year-old woman. The rhythm is now regular at about 57 bpm (RR 1.02-1.10 s) with a reproducible upright P wave in lead II before each QRS and PR about 195 ms: sinus bradycardia. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +38 degrees (normal). Repolarisation is grossly prolonged, with a very broad T wave, QT about 595 ms and Bazett QTc about 583 ms. The prior ECG 100867733 (2022-04-06) showed an irregularly irregular rhythm at about 131 bpm with no organised P waves (beat-to-beat pre-QRS correlation 0.20), i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, and a QTc of about 430 ms. Compared with that tracing the atrial fibrillation has resolved (RESOLVED_AF) and the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60), the latter consistent with her ongoing amiodarone therapy.

items.explanation: 74-year-old man with atrial flutter on apixaban 5 mg BID (order authored 2026-08-20, valid through 2027-01-04) plus aspirin and clopidogrel. Outside-records summary of 2026-08-12 documents admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (hemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. Apixaban was nonetheless re-ordered at the 8/20/2026 clinic visit and the note lists it as a current medication, with no documented review of the bleed. Anticoagulation should not continue without prescriber review of bleeding risk versus thromboembolic risk (and of concomitant aspirin/clopidogrel).

79-year-old man with atrial fibrillation on amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication (current clinic order 2026-07-12 to 2027-01-09; started at the 11/10/2025 clinic visit). His most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT about 555 ms and Bazett QTc about 565 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. This is a marked increase from the QTc of about 420 ms on the preceding ECG (108780865, 2025-06-07) before amiodarone was started. Most recent potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (both 2026-06-09) are normal.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list) was newly started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02; there is no earlier citalopram order for this patient. Because the start was on or after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was obtained on 2026-03-07, within the window, so the requirement is met (that tracing shows sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with QTc about 390 ms).

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started as an outpatient medication at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (earlier amiodarone exposure was inpatient only, in January 2025). The start falls between 9/1/2025 and 3/1/2026, so the original memo applies and an ECG was required within 30 days, i.e. by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded on 2025-11-24, within the window, so the monitoring requirement is complete (although that ECG shows a QTc of about 565 ms, which is flagged separately).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-02-12, which is on or after 9/1/2025 but before 3/1/2026, so the 30-day window of the original memo applies (due 2026-03-14). ECG 101538691 was obtained on 2026-03-08, within the window, so the requirement is satisfied; it shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QTc about 440 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (the only previous exposure was a brief inpatient order in December 2025 that had ended). Because the start was after 3/1/2026 an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-08-15. The only ECG in the chart is 106035722 from 2025-12-25, long before the start, and no ECG has been obtained since. As of 2026-09-24 the requirement is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10 and has been continued since. The start is after 3/1/2026 so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-04-24. The only ECG in the chart, 107859369, was recorded on 2026-04-29, five days after the deadline, so the requirement was not met within the required time and is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (prior exposure was inpatient only, in 2024). The start is after 3/1/2026 so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-24. No ECG for this patient exists in the chart, but the nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 and that the report was requested but not yet received. That outside tracing falls inside the required window and could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report is obtained.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was newly started as an outpatient medication at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15 (earlier haloperidol was inpatient only, in early 2025). The 14-day window of the revised memo applies, so an ECG is due by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained since the start (most recent tracing is 104253928 from 2025-03-09), but the deadline is after the 2026-09-24 evaluation date, so the requirement is not yet due.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 the clinician documented a subtherapeutic INR of 1.6 and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR is required within 7 days of a dose change made by a Cardiology Clinic clinician, i.e. by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, inside the window, so the monitoring requirement is complete.

The clinic pharmacist decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily on 2026-09-10 for a home INR of 3.4, a dose change permitted under the anticoagulation clinic standing order. The 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days of such a change, i.e. by 2026-09-17. No INR has been resulted since the change (the most recent INR in the chart is 2.7 on 2026-06-17), and the due date has passed as of the 2026-09-24 evaluation, so the follow-up INR is overdue in a 95-year-old on concurrent amiodarone.

48-year-old man with documented atrial fibrillation (encounter diagnoses 2/26/2025, 6/17/2025 and 6/23/2025; cardiology clinic notes list paroxysmal atrial fibrillation/atrial fibrillation in the problem list through the most recent visit 8/4/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (congestive heart failure - acute systolic heart failure/CHF 428.21, 428.0 - 1 point; hypertension 401.9/403.90 - 1 point); age 48, male, no diabetes, no prior stroke/TIA, no vascular disease. Score >=2 in a man meets the 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS class 1 recommendation for oral anticoagulation, but no anticoagulant is currently ordered (current clinic orders are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline only).

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (encounter diagnosis 8/22/2025; carried in the problem list of every cardiology clinic note including the most recent 6/27/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension 401.9 - 1; age 65-74 - 1; vascular disease, coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 414.01 - 1). Guidelines recommend oral anticoagulation, but the only current medication order is levothyroxine; no anticoagulant is prescribed. Documented history of hemorrhage complicating a procedure should be weighed but is not by itself a reason to withhold therapy without review.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (encounter diagnosis 3/14/2025). CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (hypertension I10/I129/401.9 - 1; age 65-74 - 1; prior ischemic stroke, cerebral infarction I639/I6340 with residual hemiplegia I69354 - 2; female sex - 1). Oral anticoagulation is strongly recommended, yet current orders are famotidine, metoprolol tartrate and levothyroxine only, and no anticoagulant appears in any clinic note medication list.

Two different oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current for this 65-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-23) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2027-01-03). The 7/15/2026 cardiology clinic note states the intent was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban was re-ordered the same day and is still listed among current medications, so both remain active. Concurrent DOACs markedly increase bleeding risk (he is also on clopidogrel); the rivaroxaban order should be stopped.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states "ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72." Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: ECG 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) and ECG 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR intervals ranging 0.35-0.72 s) with no discernible organised P waves, i.e. atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response at about 139 and 144 bpm respectively. An unspecified atrial fibrillation diagnosis was recorded at the same encounter. The documented rhythm and rate are both inconsistent with the tracings and need clinical reconciliation.

Patient is taking escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication (current clinic order 2026-07-18 to 2026-12-26, continuously prescribed since 2024). His most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT about 500 ms and Bazett-corrected QTc about 535 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. Most recent electrolytes are not contributory (potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL, both 2026-03-18). Of note, the 5/14/2024 note that started escitalopram described this same tracing as having an acceptable QT.

Patient is on citalopram 40 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication (current clinic order 2026-07-15 to 2027-01-07; citalopram has been continued since 2023). Her most recent ECG (104821039, 2023-11-10) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT about 495-500 ms and Bazett QTc about 534 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. Note also that 40 mg daily exceeds the labelled maximum citalopram dose because of dose-dependent QT prolongation. Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (2026-07-15) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (2025-03-08) are normal.

95-year-old woman on amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication (current clinic order 2026-06-17 to 2027-01-06). Her most recent ECG (101515306, 2022-04-27) shows sinus bradycardia at 57 bpm with a markedly prolonged QT of about 595 ms and Bazett QTc about 583 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. Most recent potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (both 2026-06-17) are within range, so the prolongation is not explained by electrolytes; she is also on metoprolol, and no ECG has been repeated in over four years.

interpretations.explanation: Most recent (and only) ECG, 2026-03-07. Regular narrow-complex rhythm at about 81 bpm with a consistent upright P wave in lead II before every QRS (P amplitude ~200 uV, beat-to-beat P correlation 0.99) and PR about 180 ms, i.e. normal sinus rhythm with mild sinus arrhythmia (RR 0.66-0.86 s). QRS duration 80 ms with no bundle branch block pattern; frontal QRS axis about +45 degrees (normal). QT about 335 ms at RR 0.74 s gives a Bazett QTc of roughly 390 ms, normal. No prior ECG is available for comparison. Notable because the same-day clinic note reports sinus rhythm, which this tracing confirms, despite a history of atrial fibrillation.

ECG of 2025-07-15. Regular rhythm at about 104 bpm (RR 0.58 s) with a prominent upright P wave in lead II before every QRS (P amplitude ~215 uV, P correlation 0.98) and PR about 140 ms: sinus tachycardia. QRS 94 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +38 degrees (normal). QT about 325 ms, Bazett QTc about 428 ms, normal. The prior ECG 100698634 (2025-06-20) was sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm with QRS 90 ms and QTc about 410 ms; rhythm, conduction and QTc are unchanged apart from the slower rate. Notably, despite documented paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, both tracings are in sinus rhythm.

ECG of 2024-05-21, the only tracing available. Regular rhythm at about 109 bpm (RR 0.55 s) with a consistent upright P wave in lead II before each QRS and PR about 130 ms: sinus tachycardia. QRS 90 ms, narrow, with no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +35 degrees (normal). QT about 315 ms, Bazett QTc about 424 ms, normal. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 2026-06-10 19:36, the later of two tracings that day. The ventricular response is irregularly irregular (RR intervals 0.35-0.65 s) at an average rate of about 144 bpm, with no organised P waves (pre-QRS atrial deflection ~70 uV with poor beat-to-beat reproducibility, correlation 0.45) and a fibrillatory baseline: atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response. No measurable PR interval. QRS 92 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +3 degrees (normal). QT about 290 ms, Bazett QTc about 450 ms. The earlier tracing the same day, 107914094 (17:13), showed the same rhythm - atrial fibrillation at about 139 bpm with QRS 96 ms and QTc about 450 ms - so there are no interval changes. The clinic note of the same day describing normal sinus rhythm at 72 bpm conflicts with both tracings.

ECG of 2025-08-02. Regular rhythm at about 69 bpm (RR 0.87 s, coefficient of variation 0.01) with a low-amplitude atrial deflection preceding every QRS at a fixed PR of about 125 ms; the P wave is positive in leads I and aVL but negative in II, III and aVF, suggesting a low atrial pacemaker rather than a high right atrial focus, but the rhythm is regular, 1:1 conducted and physiological. QRS 78 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about -25 degrees (normal, borderline leftward). QT about 405 ms, Bazett QTc about 435 ms, normal. The prior ECG 104232242 (2025-04-27) had the same rate-corrected intervals (QRS 78 ms, QTc about 411 ms) but showed a globally inverted limb-lead pattern consistent with arm-lead reversal; there are no qualifying changes between the tracings.

ECG of 2024-05-23, the only tracing available. Regular rhythm at about 97 bpm (RR 0.62 s) with a reproducible upright P wave in lead II before every QRS and PR about 120 ms: sinus rhythm at the upper limit of normal rate. QRS 76 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block pattern; frontal QRS axis about 0 degrees (normal). QT about 290 ms, Bazett QTc about 367 ms, normal. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 2025-12-25, the only tracing available. Regular rhythm at about 72 bpm (RR 0.83 s) with an upright P wave in lead II before every QRS and PR about 130-145 ms: normal sinus rhythm. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +22 degrees (normal). QT about 385 ms, Bazett QTc about 421 ms, normal. No prior ECG for comparison. This tracing predates the escitalopram started 2026-08-01 and therefore cannot serve as the post-initiation ECG required by clinic policy.

ECG of 2024-11-15. The ventricular response is irregularly irregular (RR intervals 0.69-1.16 s, RMSSD 288 ms) with no organised P waves - the pre-QRS atrial deflection is only about 35 uV and is not reproducible from beat to beat (correlation 0.31) - indicating atrial fibrillation with a slow ventricular response averaging about 53 bpm. No measurable PR interval. QRS 90 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +29 degrees (normal). QT about 440 ms at this slow rate, Bazett QTc about 414 ms, normal. The prior ECG 107873952 (2024-11-12) was regular sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with a well-formed 220 uV P wave and PR about 160 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new since that tracing (NEW_AF). The QTc is essentially unchanged.

ECG of 2025-03-09. Regular rhythm at about 58 bpm (RR 1.03 s) with a reproducible upright P wave in lead II before each QRS (P correlation 1.00) and PR about 110 ms: sinus bradycardia. QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +61 degrees (normal). QT about 445 ms at this slow rate, Bazett QTc about 437 ms, within normal limits. The prior ECG 106045460 (2025-03-08) was nearly identical (sinus rhythm 62 bpm, QRS 86 ms, QTc about 455 ms), so there are no qualifying changes. This tracing predates the haloperidol started 2026-09-15.

ECG of 2025-08-23, the only tracing available. Regular rhythm at about 83 bpm (RR 0.72 s, coefficient of variation <0.01) with an upright P wave in lead II before every QRS and PR about 140 ms: normal sinus rhythm. QRS 72 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +54 degrees (normal). QT about 340 ms, Bazett QTc about 401 ms, normal. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 2020-06-19. Regular rhythm at about 77 bpm (RR 0.78 s) with a large upright P wave in lead II before every QRS (about 265 uV) and PR about 148 ms: normal sinus rhythm. QRS 74 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +65 degrees (normal). QT about 385 ms, Bazett QTc about 436 ms, normal. The prior ECG 109048192 (2020-02-02) was sinus rhythm at 75 bpm but with a wider QRS of about 114 ms (still below the 120 ms criterion for bundle branch block) and a markedly prolonged QT with QTc about 590 ms. The QTc has therefore fallen by more than 60 ms (QTC_DECREASE_60); no bundle branch block is present on either tracing.

ECG of 2021-01-18. Regular rhythm at about 120 bpm (RR 0.50 s, essentially no variability) with a discrete upright P wave preceding every QRS in lead II and a biphasic P in V1; PR about 170 ms. This is sinus tachycardia. QRS 92 ms without a bundle branch block pattern; frontal axis about +50 degrees (normal). QT about 260 ms, Bazett QTc about 371 ms, normal. Compared with the prior tracing 106186980 (2016-09-16, sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, QRS 90 ms, QTc about 375 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

ECG of 2025-06-23. Regular rhythm at about 54 bpm (RR 1.10 s) with a broad upright P wave in lead II before every QRS and a prolonged PR interval of about 210-225 ms, i.e. sinus bradycardia with first-degree atrioventricular block. QRS 82 ms, narrow, with no bundle branch block (prominent q waves inferiorly and tall R waves in V3-V5 but normal duration); frontal QRS axis about 0 degrees (normal). QT about 405 ms, Bazett QTc about 387 ms, normal. The prior ECG 103042067 (2024-11-30) showed sinus bradycardia at 51 bpm with PR about 182 ms, QRS 84 ms and QTc about 377 ms; the PR has lengthened slightly into the first-degree block range, but none of the listed change categories apply.

ECG of 2025-09-13. Markedly irregular ventricular response (RR intervals 0.29-0.58 s, coefficient of variation 0.19) at an average rate of about 152 bpm, with no discernible P waves at all (pre-QRS atrial signal about 10 uV, beat-to-beat correlation 0.12): atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response. No measurable PR interval. QRS 100 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about -22 degrees (normal). QT about 255 ms, Bazett QTc about 408 ms, normal. The prior ECG 107374881 (2025-09-12, the day before) showed a regular rhythm at about 77 bpm with visible P waves and PR about 130 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new (NEW_AF); QTc is essentially unchanged.

ECG of 2025-11-23. Regular rhythm at about 73 bpm (RR 0.82 s) with a well-formed upright P wave in lead II before every QRS (about 220 uV, correlation 0.99) and PR about 165 ms: normal sinus rhythm, confirming the same-day clinic note. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +10 degrees (normal). QT about 360 ms, Bazett QTc about 396 ms, normal. The prior ECG 105362569 (2025-11-21) was also sinus rhythm (67 bpm, QRS 88 ms) but with QT about 500 ms and QTc about 527 ms, so the QTc has fallen by more than 60 ms (QTC_DECREASE_60).

ECG of 2025-02-15, the only tracing available. Regular rhythm at about 74 bpm (RR 0.81 s) with an upright P wave in lead II before every QRS and PR about 185-190 ms, at the upper limit of normal but not meeting criteria for first-degree AV block: normal sinus rhythm. QRS 88 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +61 degrees (normal). QT about 380 ms, Bazett QTc about 421 ms, normal. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 2023-06-26. Regular rhythm at about 112 bpm (RR 0.538 s with almost no variability) with a single upright P wave in leads II, III and aVF before each QRS, an isoelectric PR segment and PR about 175 ms; there is no sawtooth flutter baseline and no second atrial deflection in the ST segment, so this is sinus tachycardia rather than atrial flutter despite the documented flutter history. QRS 94 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +35 degrees (normal). QT about 280 ms, Bazett QTc about 379 ms, normal. The prior ECG 102955795 (2022-07-04) was essentially identical (sinus tachycardia 115 bpm, QRS 94 ms, QTc about 376 ms), so there are no changes.

ECG of 2025-03-14, the only tracing available. Underlying rhythm is regular at about 61 bpm (RR 0.98 s) with a broad upright P wave in lead II before each QRS and PR about 190 ms: sinus rhythm; a single premature beat with a compensatory pause accounts for the isolated short-long RR sequence and for the high RMSSD, and there is no fibrillatory baseline, so this tracing is not in atrial fibrillation despite the documented paroxysmal AF. QRS 98 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about -31 degrees (left axis deviation). QT about 385 ms, Bazett QTc about 388 ms, normal. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 2026-04-29, the only tracing available. Regular rhythm at about 69 bpm (RR 0.86 s) with a small, reproducible atrial deflection before each QRS at a fixed PR of about 135 ms: sinus rhythm. QRS 92 ms, narrow, with no bundle branch block. The frontal plane is strikingly abnormal: the P wave, QRS and T are all negative in lead I and lead II and positive in aVR, giving a measured frontal QRS axis of about -173 degrees (extreme axis); the precordial R-wave progression is normal, so this pattern most likely reflects right/left arm lead reversal rather than true extreme axis deviation or dextrocardia, and repeating the tracing with correct lead placement is advised. QT about 365 ms, Bazett QTc about 391 ms, normal. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 2023-11-10. Regular rhythm at about 70 bpm (RR 0.86 s) with an upright P wave in lead II before every QRS and PR about 150-165 ms: normal sinus rhythm. QRS 96 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +42 degrees (normal). The T waves are broad and prolonged with QT about 495 ms and Bazett QTc about 534 ms, clearly prolonged. The prior ECG 107149156 (2020-06-17) showed sinus tachycardia at 133 bpm with QT about 275 ms and QTc about 411 ms, so the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60). She remains on citalopram 40 mg daily.

ECG of 2026-03-08, the only tracing available. Regular rhythm at about 68 bpm (RR 0.88 s) with an upright P wave in lead II before every QRS and PR about 135-150 ms: normal sinus rhythm. QRS 84 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +57 degrees (normal). There is repolarisation abnormality with T-wave inversion in I, V2, V5 and V6 and a deeply negative T in V2-V3; measured QT is about 410-420 ms and the Bazett QTc is about 440 ms, i.e. borderline but below the 500 ms clinic threshold. No prior ECG for comparison. This is the post-initiation ECG for escitalopram started 2026-02-12.

ECG of 2019-01-13. Regular rhythm at about 53 bpm (RR 1.13 s) with an upright P wave in lead II before every QRS and PR about 165 ms: sinus bradycardia. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about -5 degrees (normal). QT about 380 ms, Bazett QTc about 355 ms, normal. The prior ECG 108651109 (2018-12-13) was sinus rhythm at 66 bpm with QRS 98 ms and QTc about 397 ms; the QTc change is about 40 ms, below the 60 ms threshold, and there are no other qualifying changes.

ECG of 2023-10-08. Regular sinus rhythm at about 68 bpm (RR 0.88 s) with a uniform upright P wave in lead II before each QRS and PR about 130-145 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +50 degrees (normal). The T waves are broad and late-peaking with QT about 500 ms, giving a Bazett QTc of roughly 535 ms, which is markedly prolonged. The previous ECG 100065910 (2022-11-23) was sinus rhythm at 74 bpm with QT about 330 ms and QTc about 365 ms, so the QTc has increased by well over 60 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60). This is the patient's most recent tracing and he remains on escitalopram, a QT watch-list drug.

ECG of 2022-07-13. The rhythm is now regular (RR 0.40-0.45 s, coefficient of variation 0.02) at about 141 bpm, with a reproducible low-amplitude P wave preceding each QRS and an isoelectric segment before the QRS; this is sinus tachycardia. No pacing spikes are present despite the documented pacemaker. QRS 84 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about 0 degrees (normal). QT about 270 ms, Bazett QTc about 417 ms, normal. The prior ECG 109839112 (2022-07-11) showed an irregularly irregular rhythm at about 110 bpm with no organised P waves (atrial signal about 30 uV, beat-to-beat correlation 0.41), i.e. atrial fibrillation; that atrial fibrillation has resolved on the present tracing (RESOLVED_AF). QTc is unchanged.

ECG of 2025-05-12, the only tracing available. Regular rhythm at about 82 bpm (RR 0.73 s) with an upright P wave in lead II before every QRS (correlation 0.98) and PR about 140-155 ms: normal sinus rhythm. QRS duration is about 104 ms - a nonspecific intraventricular conduction delay but below the 120 ms threshold, and without an RBBB or LBBB pattern. Frontal QRS axis about +33 degrees (normal). QT about 375 ms, Bazett QTc about 438 ms, normal. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 2022-07-16. Regular rhythm at about 91 bpm (RR 0.66 s) with a consistent upright P wave in lead II before every QRS (correlation 1.00) and PR about 165-185 ms: normal sinus rhythm. QRS 80 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about -17 degrees (normal). QT about 340 ms, Bazett QTc about 421 ms, normal. The prior ECG 102616671 (2021-05-16) was sinus rhythm at 87 bpm with QRS 84 ms and QTc about 403 ms, so there are no qualifying changes.

ECG of 2024-07-17. Regular rhythm at about 61 bpm (RR 0.98 s) with an upright P wave in lead II before every QRS and a prolonged PR of about 215-230 ms: sinus rhythm with first-degree atrioventricular block. The QRS is wide at about 132 ms with a broad monophasic R wave in leads I, aVL and V6, absence of q waves laterally and a QS complex in V1-V3 - a left bundle branch block pattern - with secondary ST-T changes. Frontal QRS axis about -20 degrees (normal). QT about 450 ms, Bazett QTc about 452 ms, mildly prolonged but below the 500 ms threshold. The prior ECG 103686933 (2024-06-03) showed the same findings (sinus rhythm 68 bpm, PR about 212 ms, QRS 130 ms with LBBB, QTc about 437 ms), so the bundle branch block is not new and there are no qualifying changes.

ECG of 2025-03-19. Regular rhythm at about 102 bpm (RR 0.59 s) with an upright P wave in lead II before every QRS (correlation 0.99) and PR about 135 ms: sinus tachycardia. QRS 88 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +45 degrees (normal). QT about 320 ms, Bazett QTc about 414 ms, normal. The prior ECG 101016166 (2025-03-18) was essentially identical (sinus tachycardia 102 bpm, QRS 84 ms, QTc about 414 ms), so there are no changes.

ECG of 2025-09-22, the only tracing available. Regular rhythm at about 66 bpm (RR 0.91 s) with an upright P wave in lead II before every QRS and PR about 150 ms: normal sinus rhythm. QRS 90 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about -19 degrees (normal). QT about 375 ms, Bazett QTc about 394 ms, normal. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 2024-04-19, the only tracing available. Regular rhythm at about 120 bpm (RR 0.50 s, coefficient of variation <0.01) with a consistent upright P wave in lead II before every QRS and PR about 135 ms: sinus tachycardia. QRS 78 ms, narrow, with no bundle branch block or fascicular pattern; frontal QRS axis about +69 degrees (normal). QT about 250 ms; Bazett QTc about 354 ms, normal. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 2021-08-23 (the later of two tracings recorded the same day). Regular rhythm at about 101 bpm with an upright P wave in lead II preceding every QRS (P amplitude ~180 uV, P correlation 0.99) and PR about 135 ms: sinus tachycardia. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +59 degrees (normal). QT about 310 ms, Bazett QTc about 400 ms, normal. The immediately preceding tracing 102910502 from the same day was essentially identical (sinus tachycardia 100 bpm, QRS 88 ms, QTc about 396 ms), so there are no interval change.

ECG of 2024-10-24. Regular rhythm at about 52 bpm (RR 1.15-1.18 s) with an upright P wave in lead II before each QRS and PR about 168 ms: sinus bradycardia. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +36 degrees (normal). QT about 440 ms at this slow rate, Bazett QTc about 407 ms, normal. The prior ECG 104629882 (2023-05-22) showed sinus rhythm at 57 bpm with one premature beat, QRS 84 ms and QTc about 393 ms; there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc. Importantly, despite a documented history of atrial fibrillation, this tracing is in sinus rhythm.

ECG of 2024-12-05 (second tracing that day). Rhythm is sinus tachycardia at about 121 bpm (RR 0.49 s) with an upright P wave in lead II before each conducted beat and PR about 150 ms; there is one premature beat with a short coupling interval. The QRS is now narrow at 90 ms with no bundle branch block. The frontal QRS axis is about +144 degrees (right axis deviation: QRS is net negative in lead I and net positive in aVF). QT about 280 ms, Bazett QTc about 400 ms, normal. The earlier tracing the same day, 106516875, showed a wide-complex rhythm at 100 bpm with a QRS of about 150 ms, a tall monophasic R wave in V1, deeply negative QRS in I/V6 and an extreme frontal axis (about -170 degrees) - a right bundle branch block type intraventricular conduction delay. That wide-complex conduction abnormality has resolved on the present tracing (RESOLVED_BUNDLE_BRANCH_BLOCK); the QTc is unchanged (about 425 to 400 ms).

ECG of 2025-11-24. Regular rhythm at about 62 bpm (RR 0.97 s) with an upright P wave in lead II before each QRS and PR about 165 ms: normal sinus rhythm; despite a history of atrial fibrillation this tracing is not in AF. QRS 96 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +67 degrees (normal). The repolarisation is markedly prolonged, with a very broad T wave, QT about 555 ms and Bazett QTc about 565 ms. The prior ECG 108780865 (2025-06-07) showed sinus bradycardia at 47 bpm with QT about 475 ms and QTc about 420 ms, so the QTc has risen by about 145 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60). The interval change coincides with amiodarone started at the 2025-11-10 clinic visit.

ECG of 2024-09-17, the only tracing available. The rhythm is irregularly irregular (RR intervals 0.39-1.09 s, coefficient of variation 0.29, RMSSD 264 ms) with no organised P waves before the QRS complexes (pre-QRS atrial deflection only ~50 uV and poorly reproducible between beats, beat-to-beat correlation 0.48) and a fibrillatory baseline: atrial fibrillation with an average ventricular rate of about 99 bpm. No measurable PR interval. QRS 82 ms, narrow, without bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about -52 degrees (left axis deviation). QT about 320 ms, Bazett QTc about 411 ms, normal. No prior ECG for comparison. The AF is consistent with the recorded diagnosis; the patient is on warfarin.

items.explanation: 74-year-old man with atrial flutter on apixaban 5 mg BID (order authored 2026-08-20, valid through 2027-01-04) plus aspirin and clopidogrel. Outside-records summary of 2026-08-12 documents admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (hemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. Apixaban was nonetheless re-ordered at the 8/20/2026 clinic visit and the note lists it as a current medication, with no documented review of the bleed. Anticoagulation should not continue without prescriber review of bleeding risk versus thromboembolic risk (and of concomitant aspirin/clopidogrel).

79-year-old man with atrial fibrillation on amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication (current clinic order 2026-07-12 to 2027-01-09; started at the 11/10/2025 clinic visit). His most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT about 555 ms and Bazett QTc about 565 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. This is a marked increase from the QTc of about 420 ms on the preceding ECG (108780865, 2025-06-07) before amiodarone was started. Most recent potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (both 2026-06-09) are normal.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list) was newly started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02; there is no earlier citalopram order for this patient. Because the start was on or after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was obtained on 2026-03-07, within the window, so the requirement is met (that tracing shows sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with QTc about 390 ms).

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started as an outpatient medication at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (earlier amiodarone exposure was inpatient only, in January 2025). The start falls between 9/1/2025 and 3/1/2026, so the original memo applies and an ECG was required within 30 days, i.e. by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded on 2025-11-24, within the window, so the monitoring requirement is complete (although that ECG shows a QTc of about 565 ms, which is flagged separately).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-02-12, which is on or after 9/1/2025 but before 3/1/2026, so the 30-day window of the original memo applies (due 2026-03-14). ECG 101538691 was obtained on 2026-03-08, within the window, so the requirement is satisfied; it shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QTc about 440 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (the only previous exposure was a brief inpatient order in December 2025 that had ended). Because the start was after 3/1/2026 an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-08-15. The only ECG in the chart is 106035722 from 2025-12-25, long before the start, and no ECG has been obtained since. As of 2026-09-24 the requirement is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10 and has been continued since. The start is after 3/1/2026 so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-04-24. The only ECG in the chart, 107859369, was recorded on 2026-04-29, five days after the deadline, so the requirement was not met within the required time and is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (prior exposure was inpatient only, in 2024). The start is after 3/1/2026 so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-24. No ECG for this patient exists in the chart, but the nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 and that the report was requested but not yet received. That outside tracing falls inside the required window and could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report is obtained.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was newly started as an outpatient medication at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15 (earlier haloperidol was inpatient only, in early 2025). The 14-day window of the revised memo applies, so an ECG is due by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained since the start (most recent tracing is 104253928 from 2025-03-09), but the deadline is after the 2026-09-24 evaluation date, so the requirement is not yet due.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 the clinician documented a subtherapeutic INR of 1.6 and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR is required within 7 days of a dose change made by a Cardiology Clinic clinician, i.e. by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, inside the window, so the monitoring requirement is complete.

The clinic pharmacist decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily on 2026-09-10 for a home INR of 3.4, a dose change permitted under the anticoagulation clinic standing order. The 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days of such a change, i.e. by 2026-09-17. No INR has been resulted since the change (the most recent INR in the chart is 2.7 on 2026-06-17), and the due date has passed as of the 2026-09-24 evaluation, so the follow-up INR is overdue in a 95-year-old on concurrent amiodarone.

48-year-old man with documented atrial fibrillation (encounter diagnoses 2/26/2025, 6/17/2025 and 6/23/2025; cardiology clinic notes list paroxysmal atrial fibrillation/atrial fibrillation in the problem list through the most recent visit 8/4/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (congestive heart failure - acute systolic heart failure/CHF 428.21, 428.0 - 1 point; hypertension 401.9/403.90 - 1 point); age 48, male, no diabetes, no prior stroke/TIA, no vascular disease. Score >=2 in a man meets the 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS class 1 recommendation for oral anticoagulation, but no anticoagulant is currently ordered (current clinic orders are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline only).

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (encounter diagnosis 8/22/2025; carried in the problem list of every cardiology clinic note including the most recent 6/27/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension 401.9 - 1; age 65-74 - 1; vascular disease, coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 414.01 - 1). Guidelines recommend oral anticoagulation, but the only current medication order is levothyroxine; no anticoagulant is prescribed. Documented history of hemorrhage complicating a procedure should be weighed but is not by itself a reason to withhold therapy without review.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (encounter diagnosis 3/14/2025). CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (hypertension I10/I129/401.9 - 1; age 65-74 - 1; prior ischemic stroke, cerebral infarction I639/I6340 with residual hemiplegia I69354 - 2; female sex - 1). Oral anticoagulation is strongly recommended, yet current orders are famotidine, metoprolol tartrate and levothyroxine only, and no anticoagulant appears in any clinic note medication list.

Two different oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current for this 65-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-23) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2027-01-03). The 7/15/2026 cardiology clinic note states the intent was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban was re-ordered the same day and is still listed among current medications, so both remain active. Concurrent DOACs markedly increase bleeding risk (he is also on clopidogrel); the rivaroxaban order should be stopped.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states "ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72." Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: ECG 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) and ECG 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR intervals ranging 0.35-0.72 s) with no discernible organised P waves, i.e. atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response at about 139 and 144 bpm respectively. An unspecified atrial fibrillation diagnosis was recorded at the same encounter. The documented rhythm and rate are both inconsistent with the tracings and need clinical reconciliation.

Patient is taking escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication (current clinic order 2026-07-18 to 2026-12-26, continuously prescribed since 2024). His most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT about 500 ms and Bazett-corrected QTc about 535 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. Most recent electrolytes are not contributory (potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL, both 2026-03-18). Of note, the 5/14/2024 note that started escitalopram described this same tracing as having an acceptable QT.

Patient is on citalopram 40 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication (current clinic order 2026-07-15 to 2027-01-07; citalopram has been continued since 2023). Her most recent ECG (104821039, 2023-11-10) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT about 495-500 ms and Bazett QTc about 534 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. Note also that 40 mg daily exceeds the labelled maximum citalopram dose because of dose-dependent QT prolongation. Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (2026-07-15) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (2025-03-08) are normal.

95-year-old woman on amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication (current clinic order 2026-06-17 to 2027-01-06). Her most recent ECG (101515306, 2022-04-27) shows sinus bradycardia at 57 bpm with a markedly prolonged QT of about 595 ms and Bazett QTc about 583 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. Most recent potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (both 2026-06-17) are within range, so the prolongation is not explained by electrolytes; she is also on metoprolol, and no ECG has been repeated in over four years.

interpretations.explanation: Most recent (and only) ECG, 2026-03-07. Oral anticoagulation is strongly recommended, yet current orders are famotidine, metoprolol tartrate and levothyroxine only, and no anticoagulant appears in any clinic note medication list.

Two different oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current for this 65-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-23) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2027-01-03). The 7/15/2026 cardiology clinic note states the intent was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban was re-ordered the same day and is still listed among current medications, so both remain active. Concurrent DOACs markedly increase bleeding risk (he is also on clopidogrel); the rivaroxaban order should be stopped.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states "ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72." Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: ECG 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) and ECG 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR intervals ranging 0.35-0.72 s) with no discernible organised P waves, i.e. atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response at about 139 and 144 bpm respectively. An unspecified atrial fibrillation diagnosis was recorded at the same encounter. The documented rhythm and rate are both inconsistent with the tracings and need clinical reconciliation.

Patient is taking escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication (current clinic order 2026-07-18 to 2026-12-26, continuously prescribed since 2024). His most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT about 500 ms and Bazett-corrected QTc about 535 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. Of note, the 5/14/2024 note that started escitalopram described this same tracing as having an acceptable QT.

interpretations.explanation: Most recent (and only) ECG, 2026-03-07. Regular narrow-complex rhythm at about 81 bpm with a consistent upright P wave in lead II before every QRS (P amplitude ~200 uV, beat-to-beat P correlation 0.99) and PR about 180 ms, i.e. normal sinus rhythm with mild sinus arrhythmia (RR 0.66-0.86 s). QRS duration 80 ms with no bundle branch block pattern; frontal QRS axis about +45 degrees (normal). QT about 335 ms at RR 0.74 s gives a Bazett QTc of roughly 390 ms, normal. No prior ECG is available for comparison. Notable because the same-day clinic note reports sinus rhythm, which this tracing confirms, despite a history of atrial fibrillation.

ECG of 2025-07-15. Regular rhythm at about 104 bpm (RR 0.58 s) with a prominent upright P wave in lead II before every QRS (P amplitude ~215 uV, P correlation 0.98) and PR about 140 ms: sinus tachycardia. QRS 94 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +38 degrees (normal). QT about 325 ms, Bazett QTc about 428 ms, normal. The prior ECG 100698634 (2025-06-20) was sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm with QRS 90 ms and QTc about 410 ms; rhythm, conduction and QTc are unchanged apart from the slower rate. Notably, despite documented paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, both tracings are in sinus rhythm.

ECG of 2024-05-21, the only tracing available. Regular rhythm at about 109 bpm (RR 0.55 s) with a consistent upright P wave in lead II before each QRS and PR about 130 ms: sinus tachycardia. QRS 90 ms, narrow, with no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +35 degrees (normal). QT about 315 ms, Bazett QTc about 424 ms, normal. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 2026-06-10 19:36, the later of two tracings that day. The ventricular response is irregularly irregular (RR intervals 0.35-0.65 s) at an average rate of about 144 bpm, with no organised P waves (pre-QRS atrial deflection ~70 uV with poor beat-to-beat reproducibility, correlation 0.45) and a fibrillatory baseline: atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response. No measurable PR interval. QRS 92 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +3 degrees (normal). QT about 290 ms, Bazett QTc about 450 ms. The earlier tracing the same day, 107914094 (17:13), showed the same rhythm - atrial fibrillation at about 139 bpm with QRS 96 ms and QTc about 450 ms - so there are no interval changes. The clinic note of the same day describing normal sinus rhythm at 72 bpm conflicts with both tracings.

ECG of 2025-08-02. Regular rhythm at about 69 bpm (RR 0.87 s, coefficient of variation 0.01) with a low-amplitude atrial deflection preceding every QRS at a fixed PR of about 125 ms; the P wave is positive in leads I and aVL but negative in II, III and aVF, suggesting a low atrial pacemaker rather than a high right atrial focus, but the rhythm is regular, 1:1 conducted and physiological. QRS 78 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about -25 degrees (normal, borderline leftward). QT about 405 ms, Bazett QTc about 435 ms, normal. The prior ECG 104232242 (2025-04-27) had the same rate-corrected intervals (QRS 78 ms, QTc about 411 ms) but showed a globally inverted limb-lead pattern consistent with arm-lead reversal; there are no qualifying changes between the tracings.

ECG of 2024-05-23, the only tracing available. Regular rhythm at about 97 bpm (RR 0.62 s) with a reproducible upright P wave in lead II before every QRS and PR about 120 ms: sinus rhythm at the upper limit of normal rate. QRS 76 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block pattern; frontal QRS axis about 0 degrees (normal). QT about 290 ms, Bazett QTc about 367 ms, normal. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 2025-12-25, the only tracing available. Regular rhythm at about 72 bpm (RR 0.83 s) with an upright P wave in lead II before every QRS and PR about 130-145 ms: normal sinus rhythm. This tracing predates the escitalopram started 2026-08-01 and therefore cannot serve as the post-initiation ECG required by clinic policy.

ECG of 2024-11-15. The ventricular response is irregularly irregular (RR intervals 0.69-1.16 s, RMSSD 288 ms) with no organised P waves - the pre-QRS atrial deflection is only about 35 uV and is not reproducible from beat to beat (correlation 0.31) - indicating atrial fibrillation with a slow ventricular response averaging about 53 bpm. No measurable PR interval. QRS 90 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +29 degrees (normal). QT about 440 ms at this slow rate, Bazett QTc about 414 ms, normal. The prior ECG 107873952 (2024-11-12) was regular sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with a well-formed 220 uV P wave and PR about 160 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new since that tracing (NEW_AF). The QTc is essentially unchanged.

ECG of 2025-03-09. Regular rhythm at about 58 bpm (RR 1.03 s) with a reproducible upright P wave in lead II before each QRS (P correlation 1.00) and PR about 110 ms: sinus bradycardia. QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +61 degrees (normal). QT about 445 ms at this slow rate, Bazett QTc about 437 ms, within normal limits. The prior ECG 106045460 (2025-03-08) was nearly identical (sinus rhythm 62 bpm, QRS 86 ms, QTc about 455 ms), so there are no qualifying changes. This tracing predates the haloperidol started 2026-09-15.

ECG of 2025-08-23, the only tracing available. Regular rhythm at about 83 bpm (RR 0.72 s, coefficient of variation <0.01) with an upright P wave in lead II before every QRS and PR about 140 ms: normal sinus rhythm. QRS 72 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +54 degrees (normal). QT about 340 ms, Bazett QTc about 401 ms, normal. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 2020-06-19. Regular rhythm at about 77 bpm (RR 0.78 s) with a large upright P wave in lead II before every QRS (about 265 uV) and PR about 148 ms: normal sinus rhythm. QRS 74 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +65 degrees (normal). QT about 385 ms, Bazett QTc about 436 ms, normal. The prior ECG 109048192 (2020-02-02) was sinus rhythm at 75 bpm but with a wider QRS of about 114 ms (still below the 120 ms criterion for bundle branch block) and a markedly prolonged QT with QTc about 590 ms. The QTc has therefore fallen by more than 60 ms (QTC_DECREASE_60); no bundle branch block is present on either tracing.

ECG of 2021-01-18. Regular rhythm at about 120 bpm (RR 0.50 s, essentially no variability) with a discrete upright P wave preceding every QRS in lead II and a biphasic P in V1; PR about 170 ms. This is sinus tachycardia. QRS 92 ms without a bundle branch block pattern; frontal axis about +50 degrees (normal). QT about 260 ms, Bazett QTc about 371 ms, normal. Compared with the prior tracing 106186980 (2016-09-16, sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, QRS 90 ms, QTc about 375 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

ECG of 2025-06-23. Regular rhythm at about 54 bpm (RR 1.10 s) with a broad upright P wave in lead II before every QRS and a prolonged PR interval of about 210-225 ms, i.e. sinus bradycardia with first-degree atrioventricular block. QRS 82 ms, narrow, with no bundle branch block (prominent q waves inferiorly and tall R waves in V3-V5 but normal duration); frontal QRS axis about 0 degrees (normal). QT about 405 ms, Bazett QTc about 387 ms, normal. The prior ECG 103042067 (2024-11-30) showed sinus bradycardia at 51 bpm with PR about 182 ms, QRS 84 ms and QTc about 377 ms; the PR has lengthened slightly into the first-degree block range, but none of the listed change categories apply.

ECG of 2025-09-13. Markedly irregular ventricular response (RR intervals 0.29-0.58 s, coefficient of variation 0.19) at an average rate of about 152 bpm, with no discernible P waves at all (pre-QRS atrial signal about 10 uV, beat-to-beat correlation 0.12): atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response. No measurable PR interval. QRS 100 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about -22 degrees (normal). QT about 255 ms, Bazett QTc about 408 ms, normal. The prior ECG 107374881 (2025-09-12, the day before) showed a regular rhythm at about 77 bpm with visible P waves and PR about 130 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new (NEW_AF); QTc is essentially unchanged.

ECG of 2025-11-23. Regular rhythm at about 73 bpm (RR 0.82 s) with a well-formed upright P wave in lead II before every QRS (about 220 uV, correlation 0.99) and PR about 165 ms: normal sinus rhythm, confirming the same-day clinic note. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +10 degrees (normal). QT about 360 ms, Bazett QTc about 396 ms, normal. The prior ECG 105362569 (2025-11-21) was also sinus rhythm (67 bpm, QRS 88 ms) but with QT about 500 ms and QTc about 527 ms, so the QTc has fallen by more than 60 ms (QTC_DECREASE_60).

ECG of 2025-02-15, the only tracing available. Regular rhythm at about 74 bpm (RR 0.81 s) with an upright P wave in lead II before every QRS and PR about 185-190 ms, at the upper limit of normal but not meeting criteria for first-degree AV block: normal sinus rhythm. QRS 88 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +61 degrees (normal). QT about 380 ms, Bazett QTc about 421 ms, normal. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 2023-06-26. Regular rhythm at about 112 bpm (RR 0.538 s with almost no variability) with a single upright P wave in leads II, III and aVF before each QRS, an isoelectric PR segment and PR about 175 ms; there is no sawtooth flutter baseline and no second atrial deflection in the ST segment, so this is sinus tachycardia rather than atrial flutter despite the documented flutter history. QRS 94 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +35 degrees (normal). QT about 280 ms, Bazett QTc about 379 ms, normal. The prior ECG 102955795 (2022-07-04) was essentially identical (sinus tachycardia 115 bpm, QRS 94 ms, QTc about 376 ms), so there are no changes.

ECG of 2025-03-14, the only tracing available. Underlying rhythm is regular at about 61 bpm (RR 0.98 s) with a broad upright P wave in lead II before each QRS and PR about 190 ms: sinus rhythm; a single premature beat with a compensatory pause accounts for the isolated short-long RR sequence and for the high RMSSD, and there is no fibrillatory baseline, so this tracing is not in atrial fibrillation despite the documented paroxysmal AF. QRS 98 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about -31 degrees (left axis deviation). QT about 385 ms, Bazett QTc about 388 ms, normal. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 2026-04-29, the only tracing available. Regular rhythm at about 69 bpm (RR 0.86 s) with a small, reproducible atrial deflection before each QRS at a fixed PR of about 135 ms: sinus rhythm. QRS 92 ms, narrow, with no bundle branch block. The frontal plane is strikingly abnormal: the P wave, QRS and T are all negative in lead I and lead II and positive in aVR, giving a measured frontal QRS axis of about -173 degrees (extreme axis); the precordial R-wave progression is normal, so this pattern most likely reflects right/left arm lead reversal rather than true extreme axis deviation or dextrocardia, and repeating the tracing with correct lead placement is advised. QT about 365 ms, Bazett QTc about 391 ms, normal. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 2023-11-10. Regular rhythm at about 70 bpm (RR 0.86 s) with an upright P wave in lead II before every QRS and PR about 150-165 ms: normal sinus rhythm. QRS 96 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal QRS axis about +42 degrees (normal). The T waves are broad and prolonged with QT about 495 ms and Bazett QTc about 534 ms, clearly prolonged. The prior ECG 107149156 (2020-06-17) showed sinus tachycardia at 133 bpm with QT about 275 ms and QTc about 411 ms, so the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60). She remains on citalopram 40 mg daily.

items.explanation: 74-year-old man with atrial flutter on apixaban 5 mg BID (order authored 2026-08-20, valid through 2027-01-04) plus aspirin and clopidogrel. Outside-records summary of 2026-08-12 documents admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (hemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. Apixaban was nonetheless re-ordered at the 8/20/2026 clinic visit and the note lists it as a current medication, with no documented review of the bleed. Anticoagulation should not continue without prescriber review of bleeding risk versus thromboembolic risk (and of concomitant aspirin/clopidogrel).

79-year-old man with atrial fibrillation on amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication (current clinic order 2026-07-12 to 2027-01-09; started at the 11/10/2025 clinic visit). His most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT about 555 ms and Bazett QTc about 565 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. This is a marked increase from the QTc of about 420 ms on the preceding ECG (108780865, 2025-06-07) before amiodarone was started. Most recent potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (both 2026-06-09) are normal.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list) was newly started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02; there is no earlier citalopram order for this patient. Because the start was on or after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was obtained on 2026-03-07, within the window, so the requirement is met (that tracing shows sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with QTc about 390 ms).

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started as an outpatient medication at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (earlier amiodarone exposure was inpatient only, in January 2025). The start falls between 9/1/2025 and 3/1/2026, so the original memo applies and an ECG was required within 30 days, i.e. by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded on 2025-11-24, within the window, so the monitoring requirement is complete (although that ECG shows a QTc of about 565 ms, which is flagged separately).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-02-12, which is on or after 9/1/2025 but before 3/1/2026, so the 30-day window of the original memo applies (due 2026-03-14). ECG 101538691 was obtained on 2026-03-08, within the window, so the requirement is satisfied; it shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QTc about 440 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (the only previous exposure was a brief inpatient order in December 2025 that had ended). Because the start was after 3/1/2026 an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-08-15. The only ECG in the chart is 106035722 from 2025-12-25, long before the start, and no ECG has been obtained since. As of 2026-09-24 the requirement is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10 and has been continued since. The start is after 3/1/2026 so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-04-24. The only ECG in the chart, 107859369, was recorded on 2026-04-29, five days after the deadline, so the requirement was not met within the required time and is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (prior exposure was inpatient only, in 2024).
